history.summary: Shiva temple in the southern settlement area of Malhar, near the Rajmahal but outside the fort precincts. Per an archaeological survey paper (IJSDR 2021), it is north-facing, also known as the Pandava-Kichak temple; the west-facing Shivalinga in the garbhagriha indicates it was originally dedicated to Shiva. The shikhara is missing and only about half the temple survives, preserved by the ASI. The entrance gate carries stone sculptures of Ganga and Yamuna riding their vahanas; a stone platform with rows of elephants and floral/mythological carving survives, and a large Ardhnarishwara sculpture found on the premises is attributed by the paper to the Kushan period (3rd century CE - the paper's claim, verify). Note: this is distinct from the separate Bhima Kichak ruins also at Malhar. Coordinates are approximate (Malhar village locality); exact temple coordinates unverified.

name: Deur Temple, Malhar
town_description: Malhar (ancient Sarabhapur, also Mallar or Mallari) is a small town in Masturi tehsil, Bilaspur district, Chhattisgarh, about 40 km by road from Bilaspur. It was a major city and capital of South Kosala in the 1st millennium CE. Excavations have revealed remains from c. 1000 BCE through the Kalachuri period, and the town is on the ASI's list of monuments of national importance; a Government of India museum houses its sculpture collection.
